name: Walmart
description: Walmart is the world’s second-largest retailer, offering both physical retail and e-commerce. Until February 2025, it was America's largest company by revenue. Groceries currently account for 50% of its sales, but the company also sells a wide range of general merchandise, through Walmart U.S., Walmart International, and Sam’s Club warehouse stores. Walmart also offers health care products and pharmacy services. Founded in 1962, the company changed its name from Wal-Mart Stores to Walmart in 2018.

name: Amazon
description: Amazon.com was incorporated in 1994; in 2026, it became the world's biggest company by revenue. It is the largest e-commerce retailer in the U.S. and a player in the grocery business, owing in part to its ownership of the Whole Foods supermarket chain. The company offers cloud services through its Amazon Web Services segment. Amazon develops and produces media content, much of which it streams through its Amazon Prime membership program; in 2021, it acquired the studio Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer (MGM). Amazon also makes and sells electronic devices including the Kindle e-book reader and Echo “smart speaker.”

name: Saudi Aramco
description: Saudi Aramco got its start in the 1930s when Standard Oil of California found large petroleum deposits while conducting operations at the behest of the government of Saudi Arabia. Today, the company is run and largely owned by the Saudi government and is at the top or near the top of the list of global energy firms when it comes to daily oil output, proven reserves, and global revenue. Headquartered in Dhahran, Aramco conducted an IPO in 2019 that it saw it make a small percentage of its shares available for purchase to the public.

name: China National Petroleum
description: China National Petroleum is one of the country’s largest oil companies, and also has a robust business as an oil field service provider. Headquartered in Beijing, CNPC was created in 1999 as part of a government reorganization of the energy sector. In recent years, it has significantly boosted its natural gas operations and has pledged to pursue green development. CNPC is also a major player in overseas exploration, particularly in the form of drilling, and has projects spanning from North America to Eastern Europe.

name: Sinopec Group
description: Sinopec Group is the holding company for China Petroleum and Chemical Corporation, a massive energy concern headquartered in Beijing. Sinopec is active in every aspect of the oil and gas business, including exploration, refining, and sales. The company is also a joint owner of numerous petrochemical ventures in areas ranging from the North Sea to Africa to Brazil. In recent years, Sinopec has become a significant player in the field of renewables, investing in projects ranging from vegetable-based jet fuel to green hydrogen plants. Its shares are listed on exchanges in Hong Kong, London, and New York.

name: UnitedHealth Group
description: UnitedHealth Group is a diversified health care company. Its four main segments are UnitedHealthcare, which offers health care coverage to employers, small businesses, and individuals; Optum Health, which provides health care delivery and management; Optum Insight, which sells health care software and provides data analysis and consulting services; and Optum Rx, which offers pharmacy benefits management and other pharmacy services. Founded in 1974, UnitedHealth has grown rapidly, organically, and through acquisitions; it is the largest U.S. health care company by revenue.
industry: Health Care: Insurance and Managed Care

name: Apple
description: Apple designs, manufactures, and sells smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables, and accessories. Its best-known products include the iPhone, the Mac line of personal computers, iPad tablets, and accessories like the Air Pods and the AppleWatch. The company’s services include Apple Music, which offers on-demand radio stations; Apple News+, a subscription news and magazine service; the streaming service Apple TV+t; and Apple Pay, a cashless payment service. Apple also distributes third-party applications for its products through its App Store.

name: CVS Health
description: Headquartered in Woonsocket, R.I., CVS Health owns the country’s largest pharmacy chain with more than 9,000 physical locations found mostly in the Northeastern U.S. The publicly traded corporation is comprised of more than 300,000 employees and offers pharmacy services, health and beauty products, convenience foods, and other services like photo printing. CVS Health didn’t start adding pharmacies to new stores until 1967, but since then has acquired large companies in the health space such as Aetna, Signify Health, and Oak Street Health to boost its primary care offerings and develop its own insurance arm. Other subsidiaries of CVS Health include benefit services manager CVS Caremark and MinuteClinic, a walk-in health clinic for vaccinations, health screenings, and other quick appointments.
industry: Health Care: Pharmacy and Other Services

name: Berkshire Hathaway
description: Berkshire Hathaway is a multi-industry conglomerate, led since 1965 by investor Warren Buffett. In May 2025, Buffett announced that he would step down as CEO by Jan. 1, 2026, to be succeeded by Greg Abel. Berkshire’s principal business lines are in the insurance, railroad freight, and utility industries, but it also owns dozens of well-known consumer-facing companies making everything from boxed chocolates to house paint. Berkshire’s many subsidiaries include insurer Geico, the railway BNSF, See’s Candies, the Dairy Queen restaurant chain, running-shoe maker Brooks, battery maker Duracell, and paint manufacturer Benjamin Moore. Berkshire Hathaway also owns a substantial portfolio of equities and other investments.

name: McKesson
description: McKesson provides health care services in the United States and internationally, operating a number of different businesses including distributing over-the-counter pharmaceutical drugs and other health-care-related products. Its prescription technology services business, meanwhile, serves biopharma and life sciences partners and works with patients to address medication challenges. Its medical-surgical solutions business offers various services to health care providers, including physician offices, surgery centers, nursing homes, hospital reference labs, and home health care agencies. McKesson was founded in 1833.

name: Volkswagen
description: Europe’s largest company, Volkswagen is a German automotive manufacturer. Founded in 1937, the brand built a global reputation with models like the Beetle, Golf, and Passat. The Porsche-Piëch family has been affiliated with Volkswagen since the patriarch Ferdinand Porsche designed the latter’s famous Beetle, and has controlled the group since the late 2000s. It is headquartered in Wolfsburg, Germany.

name: Alphabet
description: Google's parent company, Alphabet, is an American multinational technology conglomerate holding company. A few of its offerings include an advertising business; its Android phone products; and the Google Chrome web browser, search, Google Maps, and Google Photos. Alphabet also sells apps and in-app purchases through Google Play and YouTube, and offers cybersecurity, databases, and analytics. Its Google Workspace business includes cloud-based communication and collaboration tools for businesses, such as Gmail, Docs, Drive, Calendar, and Meet. In 2023, Alphabet was the world's second-largest tech company by revenue.

name: ExxonMobil Holdings
description: As the largest publicly traded oil and gas company in the U.S., Exxon Mobil engages in the exploration and production of crude oil and natural gas internationally. The company is also involved in the manufacturing, trade, transport, and sale of crude oil, natural gas, petroleum products, petrochemicals, and other specialty products. Additionally, Exon Mobil is focused on the pursuit of lower-emission business opportunities, including carbon capture and storage, hydrogen, lower-emission fuels, and lithium. Exxon Mobil was founded in 1870.

name: Toyota Motor
description: The storied Japanese company is renowned both for vehicles such as the Toyota Corolla—the world’s best-selling automobile of all time—and for its distinct management culture known as the Toyota Way, which has been the subject of countless academic studies. Headquartered in Toyota City in Japan’s Aichi prefecture, Toyota has several subsidiaries, including the Lexus luxury brand, and owns small stakes in other carmakers such as Mazda and Subaru. In recent years, it has pivoted heavily towards low-emission hybrid vehicles, which now make up more than two-thirds of its fleet.

name: China State Construction Engineering
description: China State Construction Engineering operates as an investment and construction company in China and internationally. Its business segments include housing construction, infrastructure, real estate development and investment, and design. Its vast reach also encompasses real estate development, financing, and investment; architectural design; urban planning; energy engineering; and machinery and equipment leasing. The company was founded in 1982 and is based in Beijing.

name: Cencora
description: Formerly known as AmerisourceBergen, Cencora sources and distributes pharmaceutical products. The company’s U.S. Healthcare Solutions business distributes pharmaceuticals, over-the-counter health care products, home health care supplies and equipment, and related services to acute care hospitals and health systems.

name: Shell
description: Shell was founded on April 23, 1907 following the merger of a British and a Dutch company. Since then, it has grown into one of the world’s largest vertically integrated energy companies with operations globally in oil and gas production, refining, fuel stations, energy trading, and chemicals. In recent years, it has expanded into cleaner energy, such as electric vehicle charging and renewable power. Its main long-term focus has been shifting from oil to natural gas. Shell has been based in London since 2022 but still keeps key offices in the Netherlands.

name: JPMorgan Chase
description: The largest of the “Big Four” banks in the U.S., JPMorgan Chase is at the center of the American financial system through its core offerings of consumer and community banking, commercial and investment banking, and asset and wealth management. The towering institution has its roots in different companies, including financial tycoon J.P. Morgan’s firm, and Chase Manhattan, with which it merged in 2000. Jamie Dimon has served as CEO since late 2005, shepherding the bank through the Global Financial Crisis. The question of who will succeed him has become one of the most closely watched stories in the business world, though Dimon has downplayed any intention of stepping down in the near term.

name: Costco Wholesale
description: Costco Wholesale is known for its operation of membership warehouses globally, along with its e-commerce websites. The retailer offers branded and private-label products in a range of merchandise categories, including groceries, and is also responsible for gas sales, pharmaceutics, hearing-aid centers, and tire installation centers, as well as various online services. Costco was founded in 1976.

name: Cigna Group
description: With roots dating back to 1792, the Cigna Group is an insurance and related services company serving millions of clients in the United States. Its Evernorth Health Services branch offers pharmacy benefits, home delivery, distribution, management solutions for plans, and health care providers. Meanwhile, the company’s Cigna Healthcare segment provides medical, behavioral health, dental, and other products to customers. In 2023, the business underwent a rebrand; Cigna Corp. changed its name to the Cigna Group, and its two segments became the primary business units.
industry: Health Care: Pharmacy and Other Services

name: Microsoft
description: Routinely ranked as one of the world’s most valuable companies by market capitalization, the software giant makes the popular Windows PC operating system and the Microsoft 365 suite of business productivity software. It also runs the Microsoft Azure cloud computing service, and owns the Xbox gaming platform, the code repository GitHub, and the professional social network LinkedIn. Cofounded by Bill Gates in 1975, Microsoft operates data centers around the globe to support its cloud computing services. In recent years, Microsoft has been at the forefront of the generative AI revolution through its partnership with OpenAI, its Copilot-branded AI applications, and its own AI models produced in-house.

name: Trafigura Group
description: Get insights into Trafigura Group including business profile, stock information, news, and rankings from Fortune.

name: Glencore
description: Swiss mining, energy and commodity trading giant Glencore is a global natural resources company with operations around the world in multiple markets. It produces and markets key materials including copper, coal, zinc and oil, playing a vital role in global supply chains.

name: Cardinal Health
description: Cardinal Health is a U.S. health care services and products company operating across over 30 countries as of 2025. The business provides customized solutions for hospitals, health care systems, pharmacies, surgery centers, clinical laboratories, and patients at home. The medical giant distributes generic and specialty pharmaceuticals, as well as medical, surgical, and laboratory products. Cardinal Health’s history dates back to 1971, in its founding as Cardinal Foods; in 1979, the company switched industries from food to health care, changing its name to Cardinal Distribution.

name: Industrial & Commercial Bank of China
description: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC) is the world’s largest bank by assets, with $6.3 trillion in assets as of mid-2024, according to S&P Global. The bank provides a wide range of personal and commercial banking services, including advising and M&A, and does business in 45 countries around the world. Founded in 1984, ICBC, like other Chinese banks launched in that era, was born out of efforts to reform and modernize the Chinese economy. In 2006, ICBC shares began to trade on the Shanghai and Hong Kong stock exchanges.

name: Samsung Electronics
description: Korea-based Samsung is the world's second-largest seller of electronics, trailing only Apple. As of August 2024, about 66% of its revenue comes from its devices segment, which includes home appliances and mobile phones. Samsung’s other segments include semiconductors (25% of revenue); display panel products, such as televisions (12%); and Harman, a maker of audio and automotive technology (5%). Incorporated in 1969, Samsung became a public company in 1975.

name: Hon Hai Precision Industry
description: Hon Hai Precision Industry is better known as Foxconn, the name it uses outside China/Taiwan. Hon Hai is the world’s largest manufacturer of electronics, and one of its largest employers, with 1.2 million workers in China, India, Japan, Malaysia, and the U.S., among other countries. Its business is divided into four segments: consumer electronics, cloud and networking, computing products and components, and others. Hon Tai manufactures about 70% of Apple’s iPhones, and assembles products for Microsoft, Amazon, and others. Founded in 1974, Ho Hai began trading publicly in 1991.

name: Chevron
description: Chevron is the second-largest integrated energy giant that’s based in the U.S., with an exploration and production arm as well as a refining and retail segment. Its products are sold at more than 8,000 Chevron and Texaco gas stations in the U.S. As an oil major, its operations also span the globe. The company changed its name to Chevron from ChevronTexaco in 2005.

name: Agricultural Bank of China
description: One of China’s “Big Four” banks, the Agricultural Bank of China has $5.6 trillion in assets as of August 2024, making it the world’s second-largest bank by assets, according to S&P Global. The bank offers both personal and business banking, with 52% of its revenues from retail customers and 39% from corporate clients. Founded in 1952, the bank was reestablished in 1979 as part of China’s economic reforms. In 2010, its dual initial public offering in Hong Kong and Shanghai raised $22.5 billion, the largest IPO in history at that time.

name: China Construction Bank
description: China Construction Bank (CCB) is the world’s third-largest bank by assets as of August 2024, with $5.4 trillion in assets, according to S&P Global. CCB serves 10.8 million corporate customers and 757 million retail customers in 31 countries and territories. The bank dates its history to 1954, when it was founded as the People’s Construction Bank of China; it was reestablished in 1979 as part of a nationwide economic reform. CCB began trading on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2005 and in Shanghai in 2007.

name: TotalEnergies
description: TotalEnergies is a global energy company based in France, operating across the entire energy value chain. Originally focused on oil and gas, it has expanded into electricity, renewables, and low-carbon solutions. Today, TotalEnergies is actively investing in solar, wind, hydrogen, and electric mobility as part of its transition to cleaner energy.

name: BP
description: BP is an integrated global energy company headquartered in London, specializing in oil and gas exploration, production, refining, and renewable energy investments. Founded over a century ago, BP plays a major role in providing energy solutions worldwide with significant operations in Europe, the United States, and Asia.

name: Bank of America
description: Bank of America, whose lineage traces back to 1784, offers banking and financial services products for consumers, businesses, governments, and investors through its consumer banking, global wealth and investment management, global banking, and global markets segments. In 2026, it was the second-largest bank by revenue in the U.S. behind JPMorgan Chase.

name: General Motors
description: General Motors, founded in 1908, was the largest automaker by revenue in the U.S. in 2024. It manufactures cars, trucks, SUVs, crossovers, and commercial vehicles for its Buick, Cadillac, Chevrolet, GMC, Baojun, and Wuling brands. It wholly owns the self-driving car company Cruise, which it fully acquired in February 2025, and plans to use its technology to develop GM driver assistance technology.

name: Ford Motor
description: Ford Motor, founded in 1903, was the second-largest automaker by revenue in the U.S. in 2024. It manufactures cars, trucks, and commercial vehicles, and owns the luxury car brand Lincoln. Ford entered the electric vehicle market in the late 1990s with its Ford Ranger EV and has since expanded its EV lineup to include the F-150 Lightning pickup truck and the Mustang Mach-E SUV.

name: Elevance Health
description: Elevance Health is a health benefits provider, offering health care coverage and specialty insurance, such as dental, vision, and life. It also operates a pharmacy service and prescription delivery business. Elevance Health was formerly known as Anthem, and does business under its Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, Wellpoint, and Carelon brands.
industry: Health Care: Insurance and Managed Care

name: Bank of China
description: Founded in 1912, Bank of China is the country’s oldest continuously operating bank. In 1994 it was restructured into a wholly state-owned commercial bank; it has branches across the Chinese mainland as well as in 62 countries and regions. It operates through six segments: corporate banking, personal banking, treasury operations, investment banking, insurance, and other (including debt-to-equity swaps, and an aircraft and financial leasing business).

name: Citigroup
description: Citigroup offers financial products and services globally to retail customers, businesses, governments, and investors through five business lines: services, markets, banking and international, wealth, and U.S. personal banking. In 2023, it was the third-largest bank by revenue in the U.S. behind Bank of America and JPMorgan Chase.

name: Stellantis
description: Stellantis is a global automaker formed in 2021 through the merger of PSA Group and Fiat Chrysler. It operates 14 iconic brands including Jeep, Peugeot, Fiat, and Chrysler with a worldwide presence. Headquartered in the Netherlands, the company focuses on electrification, innovation and sustainable mobility.

name: Meta Platforms
description: Founded in 2004 as Facebook, Meta operates the world’s largest social media platforms and has heavily influenced the development of the internet over the past two decades through its pioneering use of personal data collection and targeted advertising. Meta’s products include Facebook, image-sharing app Instagram, and messaging platforms Messenger and WhatsApp; together, they enable users to keep in touch, share images and videos, and buy and sell goods. Meta’s Reality Labs segment develops virtual-reality-related consumer hardware and software, while Meta AI develops artificial intelligence tools including language-processing models. Facebook renamed itself Meta in 2021.

name: Centene
description: Centene is the largest Medicaid insurer in the U.S. as of 2026. The company works with programs in the public and private sector to provide health care services to the underinsured and uninsured, military veterans, and commercial organizations. Programs it serves include Medicaid and Medicare plans, Medicare prescription drug plans, the Health Insurance Marketplace, and Tricare plans. It also operates its own health care and dental clinics and pharmacies. In 2024, Centene pledged to help build nearly $1 billion of affordable housing and drive better health outcomes for its members.
industry: Health Care: Insurance and Managed Care

name: China Railway Engineering Group
description: The 130-year-old China Railway Engineering Group Ltd. (known as CREC) is one of the world’s largest construction and engineering contractors. It does infrastructure construction, industrial equipment manufacturing, scientific research and consulting, real estate development, and resources development. It began in the late 19th century when China Shanhaiguan Manufactory (now a subsidiary of CREC) was set up to manufacture railway tracks and metal bridges for the first railway project designed and constructed by the Chinese.

name: JD.com
description: Incorporated in 2006, JD.com has evolved from a leading e-commerce platform into a technology and services provider offering computers, communication, and consumer electronics products, as well as home appliances; it also sells general merchandise ranging from cosmetics and baby products to furniture and car accessories. Formerly known as 360buy Jingdong, the company changed its name to JD.com in January 2014.

name: China Life Insurance
description: China Life Insurance is a life, health, and accident insurance company in China. It offers critical illness and accident protection and annuity, pension, security, and medical insurance products. The Beijing-based company was founded in 1949 and operates as a subsidiary of China Life Insurance (Group) Company.

name: Home Depot
description: Home Depot is the world’s largest home improvement retailer, operating almost 2,500 superstores in all 50 U.S. states. Home Depot sells items including appliances, tools, and hardware in its stores and online. As of 2026, it employed 472,000 associates, who are known for wearing distinctive orange uniform aprons. To expand beyond stores and e-commerce, Home Depot has invested billions in professional builder and contractor businesses. In 2024, it acquired SRS Distribution, a large distributor of building products. The deal was valued at $18.25 billion and is the largest in the retailer’s history.

name: Ping An Insurance
description: Ping An is one of China’s largest insurers, with about 240 million retail consumers across the country. Ping An's “Smart Verification” and “Smart Fast Claim” services now make its enrolment and claims processing more efficient. AI-driven tools are also reducing diagnostic times in rural areas.

name: Mercedes-Benz Group
description: Mercedes-Benz Group is recognized for its premium vehicles and innovative mobility solutions. The company develops, produces and markets passenger cars and vans under the Mercedes-Benz and smart brands. Alongside its core vehicle business, the group supports electrification, digitalization and sustainable mobility initiatives across its global operations.

name: BMW Group
description: BMW Group is a global manufacturer of premium automobiles and motorcycles with iconic brands including BMW, MINI and Rolls-Royce. Headquartered in Munich, the company operates worldwide.

name: Fannie Mae
description: The Federal National Mortgage Association, or Fannie Mae, is a major player in the secondary mortgage market. The company buys housing loans from issuers and either holds them or packages them into securities it sells to investors. Founded in 1938 as part of the New Deal, Fannie Mae became a shareholder-owned corporation in 1968. In 2008, in the wake of the Global Financial Crisis and a nationwide crash in housing values, Fannie Mae was delisted from the New York Stock Exchange and entered government conservatorship. It returned to profitability in 2012.

name: China Railway Construction
description: Founded in 1948, the China Railway Construction Corporation is a civil engineering and construction company, building and maintaining railways, highways, urban rail transport, housing, bridges, tunnels, and other such projects in mainland China. It provides planning, design, manufacturing, and real estate development services, as well as construction. It operates as a subsidiary of China Railway Construction Corporation Group.

name: Walgreens Boots Alliance
description: Walgreens Boots Alliance is a global health care, pharmacy, and retail company. It operates tens of thousands of retail locations under the Walgreens and Duane Reade names in the U.S.; Boots in the U.K., Ireland, and Thailand; and Benavides in Mexico. The company’s health care segment owns VillageMD, a health care provider with primary care, specialty care, and urgent care divisions; CareCentrix, a home health care provider; and Shields, a hospital pharmacy system. Walgreens Boots Alliance stock became a component of the Dow Jones industrial average in 2018; in March 2025, it reached a deal to go private in a sale to Sycamore Partners.

name: Kroger
description: Kroger operates thousands of U.S. supermarkets. Brands it operates include Kroger, Ralphs, and Fred Meyer. In addition to more than 2,600 grocery stores, Kroger has thousands of fuel centers and pharmacies, and employs 400,000 associates across the U.S. Kroger has a growing digital business that includes grocery orders through its Pickup program (formerly known as Clicklist). The company’s recent expansion efforts include investing in more convenience meals and expanding Mercado, a new Hispanic-inspired brand, to serve a growing demographic.

name: BNP Paribas
description: Formed in 2000 after retail bank Banque Nationale de Paris’s hostile takeover of Paribas, its largest two divisions reflect its twin origins—on the one side consumer and commercial banking focused on its home market of France, alongside Belgium, Italy and Luxembourg, and on the other global corporate and institutional banking. Paris-based BNP Paribas also has a smaller division, focused on insurance, pensions, wealth and asset management, and private banking.

name: Banco Santander
description: Banco Santander is one of Europe's largest financial businesses, headquartered in Spain and active in key markets across Europe and the Americas. Operating across retail, commercial, and corporate and investment banking, as well as in wealth management, insurance, and payments, the bank is recognized for its broad international reach and customer-focused financial solutions.

name: HSBC Holdings
description: Scotsman Thomas Sutherland founded HSBC in Hong Kong in March 1865, opening its first office in Shanghai the following month. The bank's purpose was to support local Asian and global trade in key commodities such as tea, cotton, silk, and sugar. HSBC expanded into investment banking and into new retail markets, including the U.K., with its 1992 acquisition of Midland Bank and the US through Marine Midland. Although headquartered in London, its strategic growth is focused on Asia and international clients, with renewed expansion in major Asian markets.

name: Phillips 66
description: Phillips 66 is a multinational energy company focused on refining, midstream, chemicals, and marketing. As of 2026, Phillips 66 operates ten crude oil refineries in the U.S. Its midstream business focuses on crude oil and refined products, as well as collecting and processing natural gas. The company produces chemicals for various uses in the automotive, pharmaceutical, home, and electronics industries. The marketing arm includes 7,200 fuel stations with Phillips 66, Conoco, and 76 branding.

name: China Mobile Communications
description: China Mobile Communications is the world’s largest mobile network operator by total number of subscribers, with 995.6 million as of April 2024. It is the world’s second-largest telecommunications company by market capitalization. Through its subsidiaries, China Mobile Communications operates in LTE/4G mobile telecommunication and fixed-line telecommunications businesses. The company was founded in 1997 as China Mobile Communications Corporation and changed its name to China Mobile Communications Group in 2017. The enterprise is state-owned and controlled by the government of the People’s Republic of China. It is also a public company listed on the NYSE and the Hong Kong stock exchange.

name: Honda Motor
description: Honda Motor was founded in Japan in 1946 as a bicycle auxiliary engine manufacturer. As of mid-2024, the company is the world’s largest motorcycle manufacturer as well as a major global builder and seller of automobiles. Honda Motor also develops, manufactures, and distributes power equipment, personal watercraft, robotics, jet engines, and other products internationally.

name: Marathon Petroleum
description: Marathon Petroleum is a petroleum and energy refining, processing, and marketing company. Until 2011, it was a fully owned subsidiary of Marathon Oil. MPC operates the largest petroleum refining system in the U.S. as of 2026. The marketing arm includes Marathon-branded retail outlets—gas stations offering Marathon gasoline, plus car washing services and convenience store items. In addition to its refining and fuel businesses, the company makes ingredients for household items such as carpeting and PVC pipes. Through a partnership with MPLX, Marathon Petroleum provides fuel logistics and distribution services.

name: China Communications Construction
description: China Communications Construction is an engineering and construction company primarily engaged in designing, building, operating, and managing municipal infrastructure such as bridges, railways, ports, and related projects. The company is based in Beijing and was incorporated in 2006. It operates as a subsidiary of China Communications Construction Group (Limited) and has operations in mainland China, Australia, Hong Kong, Africa, the Middle East, and Southeast Asia.

name: CITIC Group
description: Formerly known as China International Trust and Investment Corporation, CITIC Group is a transnational company that operates financial, banking, manufacturing, and telecommunication services through its 44 subsidiaries.

name: Alibaba Group Holding
description: Founded in 1999, Alibaba Group Holding provides technology infrastructure and marketing reach to help merchants, brands, retailers, and other businesses engage with users and customers. The company operates the digital retail platform Taobao and the online wholesale marketplace Alibaba.com, among others. It also provides storage, network, security, database, and IoT services, as well as hardware, software license and installation, and application development and maintenance services. The company is based in Hangzhou.

name: Verizon Communications
description: Verizon Communications is a telecommunications conglomerate providing telephone and internet services to consumers and businesses, along with wire-line internet in the Northeast through its fiber-optic network, Verizon Fios. Originating as Bell Atlantic Corp. in 1984, it merged with GTE Corp. in 2000 to become Verizon Communications. Its stock is a component of the Dow Jones industrial average.

name: China National Offshore Oil
description: China National Offshore Oil is an investment holding company which engages in oil and gas exploration and production in China and internationally. It is also involved in the refining and marketing of oil and petrochemical products, technical and financial services, and natural gas and power generation, as well as offshore wind power business. Founded in 1982, the company is state-owned.

name: Nvidia
description: Nvidia is a leading producer of chips used in artificial intelligence and, therefore, has become a critical component in the business sectors that its products power. In 2026, Nvidia has solidified its position as the most valuable company in the world. In recent years, the company has become the top supplier of chips used in data centers for the data-intensive job of training and running AI models. Nvidia is also a big seller of graphics chips for video game consoles and high-end personal computers, and chips used by the automotive industry in new cars. Nvidia was incorporated in 1993.

name: China Resources
description: China Resources, a subsidiary of China Resources Company Limited, distributes food, beverages, health care products, apparel, and other consumer goods. China Resources also offers medical devices and pharmaceutical drugs, and engages in real estate development, sale of natural gas, and other businesses.

name: Hyundai Motor
description: Hyundai Motor manufactures and distributes motor vehicles and parts. The company offers hybrid and electric cars as well as SUVs, trucks, vans, and commercial vehicles. Its Ulsan, South Korea, automotive production plant is the world’s largest and can manufacture 1.5 million cars per year.

name: Electricité de France
description: Commonly known as EDF, the French utility company generates, distributes and supplies electricity across Europe, as well as in smaller operations across the Americas, Africa and Asia. The company is structured as a private company but is fully owned by the state. It is scaling back its gas-fired generation, and phasing out its coal-fired generation completely by 2027.

name: Goldman Sachs Group
description: Goldman Sachs Group is a global investment banking, securities, and investment management firm. It caters to corporations, financial institutions, and high-net-worth individuals. In 2023, it was the world’s second-largest investment bank by revenue. In 2019, Goldman partnered with Apple to introduce the Apple credit card. Almost four years later, the bank was looking for an exit from the arrangement, part of its efforts to scale back its retail ambitions.

name: Wells Fargo
description: Wells Fargo was among the top six U.S. banks in terms of total assets in 2026. It provides consumer, commercial, corporate, and investment banking services, as well as wealth and investment management.

name: Deutsche Telekom
description: Germany’s Deutsche Telekom is one of the world's largest integrated telecommunications companies. It holds a dominant position in its primary market, Germany, and a strong presence across central and Eastern Europe and the United States. The Bonn-headquartered group also has a substantial, global business-to-business operation leveraging its infrastructure, with services in growth areas like cloud storage and data centers, cybersecurity, the internet of things and digital transformation.

name: China Baowu Steel Group
description: Formerly known as Baosteel Group Corporation, the state-owned iron and steel manufacturing company China Baowu Steel Group was founded in 1993. It offers carbon, stainless, and other kinds of steel. It also provides digital design and consulting services, and engages in mineral resources trading and logistics.

name: Valero Energy
description: Valero Energy is an oil refiner with operations in the U.S., Canada, Latin America, and Europe. Founded in 1980, the company sells gasoline, diesel, and ethanol through outlets under the Valero, Beacon, Diamond Shamrock, Shamrock, Texaco, and Ultramar brands.

name: Comcast
description: Comcast, a telecommunications conglomerate, is among the world’s largest broadcasting and cable TV companies by revenue. In 2026, Comcast Cable was the leading provider of cable internet access in the U.S., under the Xfinity brand. Comcast’s NBCUniversal division includes the television network NBC and film studio Universal Pictures. In January 2026, Comcast completed the spin off of its cable networks including USA, CNBC, MSNBC, Oxygen, E!, Syfy, and Golf Channel into an independent, publicly traded company named Versant Media Group.

name: Allianz
description: Munich-based Allianz offers a broad range of insurance and financial services and manages significant assets worldwide. Known for its strong financial performance and commitment to sustainability, Allianz is a key player in the insurance industry.

name: State Farm Insurance
description: State Farm is one of the U.S.’s largest providers of home and auto insurance, with 96 million policies and accounts in force as of 2025. A mutual insurance company, State Farm is not publicly traded, and is instead owned by its policyholders. The company is made up of 14 property-casualty insurance companies and two life insurance companies. As of 2026, more than 60% of State Farm’s business is auto insurance and 30% homeowners insurance; the remainder of its revenue comes from life insurance and small health-insurance and wealth-management businesses.

name: AT&T
description: AT&T is among the world’s largest telecommunications companies, offering wireless communications, broadband internet, and entertainment services. The company held a decades-long telephone monopoly in the U.S. before a 1982 antitrust settlement broke it into parts. In 2023, AT&T was the world’s largest telecommunications company by revenue. In 2022, AT&T finished merging its spinoff WarnerMedia with Discovery, a reorganization that resulted in the creation of Warner Bros. Discovery.

name: Mitsubishi
description: Mitsubishi engages in the development, production, and financing of natural gas/oil, industrial materials, chemicals, mineral resources, automotive and mobility, food and consumer products, power solutions, and urban development worldwide. The company was incorporated in 1950 and is headquartered in Tokyo.

name: Freddie Mac
description: Freddie Mac is a government-backed enterprise established to provide the U.S. housing market with liquidity, stability, and affordability. It pools mortgages that it buys from lenders and sells them to investors as mortgage-backed securities. This process increases the funds available for mortgage lending, which in turn supports new home purchases. Freddie Mac provides competition to—and serves a similar purpose as—Fannie Mae.

name: Hengli Group
description: Hengli Group and its subsidiaries operate oil refining, petrochemical, polyester materials, and textile businesses in China. Founded in 1994 as Wujiang Huayi Textile, the company changed its name to Hengli Group in 2023. It’s based in Suzhou, China.

name: Shandong Energy Group
description: Shandong Energy Group, is the world's largest clean-energy supplier, but also mines and distributes coal and other coal products. It operates offshore wind and coal-fired power facilities. The company changed its name from Yankuang Group in 2020.

name: Huawei Investment & Holding
description: Get insights into Huawei Investment & Holding including business profile, stock information, news, and rankings from Fortune.

name: China Southern Power Grid
description: China Southern Power Grid constructs and operates power grids across the Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, Guizhou, and Hainan provinces of China, as well as in some countries in Southeast Asia. The company supplies power to nearly 300 million people.

name: Humana
description: A health insurance company, Humana is one of the largest administrators of Medicare Advantage, a U.S. government program that provides health care to older Americans via private insurers. Humana plans are available in nearly 3,000 U.S. counties, the most of any Medicare Advantage provider. Humana also runs state-based Medicaid plans for lower-income Americans; CenterWell primary care centers for seniors; as well as home health and hospice businesses.
industry: Health Care: Insurance and Managed Care

name: China Minmetals
description: China Minmetals acquires and explores metal and mineral resources in China. It is also involved in metallurgical engineering, construction, trade and logistics, finance, and real estate development. Formerly known as China Minmetals Corp. Ltd., the company changed its name to China Minmetals Corporation in January 2012. It was founded in 1950 and is based in Beijing.

name: Gazprom
description: Gazprom is a Russian state-owned natural gas company, headquartered in Saint Petersburg. The business is vertically integrated from exploration and extraction, through to processing, distribution, supply and gas-generated electricity production. Western sanctions and European policy shifts have redirected Gazprom's exports away from Europe and towards Asia.

name: Reliance Industries
description: Reliance Industries is a conglomerate whose primary business is hydrocarbon exploration and production; its other focuses include manufacturing fabric, running various types of retail stores, and operating media and entertainment platforms. Incorporated in 1973, the company is based in Mumbai.

name: Société Générale
description: France’s emperor Napoleon III signed Société Générale into existence in 1864, and the company has been a major presence in the country’s economy ever since with headquarters in the heart of Paris's financial district. Now a multifaceted financial services company, France remains the group's major retail banking market, but it has extensive and diverse international operations including corporate and investment banking, insurance, leasing, consumer finance, and global transaction banking, in over 60 countries.

name: Rosneft Oil
description: Founded in 1993 as a Russian state enterprise and incorporated in 1995, Rosneft Oil Company is involved in oil and gas exploration, production, refining, and retail operations. Still majority-owned by the Russian government, Moscow-headquartered Rosneft experienced significant disruption following the 2022 invasion of Ukraine as Western governments imposed sanctions and placed some of its assets abroad under trusteeship.

name: BYD
description: BYD, famously backed by Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway, is arguably China’s biggest EV success story, dethroning U.S. carmaker Tesla as the world’s top seller of battery electric vehicles in the final quarter of 2023. Yet the company’s experience with battery production could be BYD’s secret sauce, giving it higher margins by consolidating its supply chains. The company is now starting to expand overseas.

name: China Energy Investment
description: China Energy Investment produces and and sells coal in China, and has businesses focused on power generation, coal chemicals, industrial finance, technology and environmental protection, and transportation. Formerly known as Shenhua Group, it was founded in 1995 and is based in Beijing.

name: Morgan Stanley
description: Morgan Stanley is an investment bank and financial services firm. Its revenues are split between securities and wealth management; its securities business includes investment banking, underwriting, and advice on mergers and acquisitions. Its prominent subsidiaries include the self-directed investing platform E*Trade and the investment management firm Eaton Vance.

name: Target
description: Target is a mass-market retail chain with more than 2,000 stores in the U.S. as of 2026. Beauty and household items make up nearly a third of Target’s sales, followed by groceries and home furnishings. Most of Target’s sales occur in its stores, with about 20% originating online. About a third of its sales come from Target-owned brands. It also partners with Starbucks and CVS, which operate outlets in Target stores. The company’s origins trace back to 1902 and the beginnings of what became the Dayton-Hudson department store company. The first Target opened in 1962.

name: Life Insurance Corp. of India
description: Life Insurance Corp. of India is a state-owned company, which was created in 1956 after India's parliament passed the Life Insurance Corporation Act.

name: Equinor
description: Originally called Statoil, Equinor was established in 1972 by the Norwegian government, which retains a majority stake in the business. Headquartered in Stavanger, Norway, Equinor is primarily involved in oil and gas exploration and production, as well as energy trading, distribution and marketing, but has significantly expanded in renewable energy, particularly offshore wind. The company has expanded internationally, with direct operations in Brazil, the U.S., the U.K. and Poland, and a presence in about 25 more countries.

name: Nestlé
description: Switzerland-based Nestlé is the world's largest food and beverage company, offering a diverse portfolio of products sold in over 185 countries. Nestlé focuses on innovation and sustainability with a diverse portfolio of brands including Nespresso, KitKat, Perrier and Maggi. The company's range spans coffee, confectionery, bottled water, baby food, dairy, culinary products, health science offerings, and pet nutrition.

name: Xiamen C&D
description: Xiamen oversees supply-chain and real estate development businesses in China and globally. The company was founded in 1980 and is based in Xiamen, China.

name: StoneX Group
description: StoneX Group connects companies and investors to markets worldwide. Its offerings include a wide range of trading products, execution of trades on futures exchanges, brokering of foreign currencies, and services that underpin the buying and selling of precious metals. Formerly known as INTL FCStone, the company was founded in 1924. It changed its name to StoneX Group in 2020.

name: Sberbank
description: Sberbank is Russia’s largest bank, offering retail and corporate banking, loans, deposits, credit cards, mortgages, and investment services. It operates an extensive branch and digital network, serving millions of customers, and plays a key role in Russia’s financial sector.

name: AXA
description: AXA traces its origins to early 19th-century France, where it began as a small mutual insurer. Rising through a series of acquisitions, it became the country's largest insurer by the early 1990s, when it also began expanding abroad. The French insurance business still accounts for a sizeable share of revenue but most of the group's revenue is generated elsewhere, driven by its operations in the rest of Europe, Asia-Pacific and North America. Although it has large asset management and health insurance businesses, its main activities remain property and casualty and life insurance. AXA is headquartered in Paris.

name: ENI
description: Italian multinational energy giant ENI operates across the oil and gas value chain, from upstream through to petrochemicals. Enel is Italy's leading gas supplier and trader with power generation and retail supply businesses for both gas and electricity, and has been expanding into renewables, biofuels, and circular chemistry. The Rome-headquartered group operates in over 60 countries.

name: Bosch Group
description: German industrial and technology conglomerate Bosch manufactures power tools, boilers, industrial hydraulics systems, home appliances and industrial machines, among other things. The company has grown into one of the world's largest suppliers of automotive components. Bosch was founded by Robert Bosch in 1886 and remains a privately owned company. It is headquartered in Gerlingen, Germany.

name: Tesla
description: Tesla is a maker of electric vehicles and energy generation and supply systems. It is the largest manufacturer of electric cars in the U.S., and, with China’s BYD, one of the two largest makers of EVs globally. Tesla was founded in 2003; Elon Musk became the company’s largest shareholder the following year.

name: China Post Group
description: China Post Group operates China's postal and express parcel service as well as financial services businesses, focusing on banking, insurance, and securities work. The company was founded in 1995 and is based in Beijing.

name: Royal Ahold Delhaize
description: Ahold Delhaize is a Netherlands-based multinational that operates more than a dozen leading supermarket chains, grocery wholesalers and e-commerce brands. These include Belgium’s Delhaize—founded in 1867 and the pioneer of self-service supermarkets in Europe—the Netherlands' Albert Heijn, Romania’s Mega Image, and several major grocery chains in the U.S. where the majority of its revenue is generated. It also has substantial retail operations in other European countries and a joint venture business based in Indonesia. Ahold Delhaize is headquartered in Zaandam, near Amsterdam.

name: Dell Technologies
description: Founded by Michael Dell in his dorm room at the University of Texas at Austin in 1984, the pioneering personal computer company made its mark by selling affordable PCs directly to consumers. The company’s offerings grew to include televisions and cameras, and by the early 2000s it came to dominate the consumer electronics market. Dell Computer went private in 2013, when Michael Dell and the private equity firm Silver Lake Partners purchased it for $25 billion; the company returned to public markets in 2018 as Dell Technologies. In 2016 the company and an investment firm acquired data storage provider EMC for $67 billion—at the time the biggest tech deal in history. In May 2025, amid growing demand for artificial intelligence systems, Dell unveiled new AI servers powered by Nvidia chips.

name: REWE Group
description: REWE Group is a leading German retail and tourism cooperative, founded in 1927 by 17 buying cooperatives aiming to leverage collective purchasing power. Headquartered in Cologne, REWE has significant operations across Europe in grocery, convenience, DIY/garden, and drugstore retail. Flagship brands include supermarket brands REWE in Germany, BILLA and PENNY in Austria and Central/Eastern Europe, alongside Toom Baumarkt (DIY), BIPA (Austria), and Lekkerland (wholesale). Its travel and tourism arm, DERTOUR Group, operates brands such as DERTOUR and Kuoni. The company also runs specialist e-commerce brands for wine (Weinfreunde), pet supplies (ZooRoyal), and more.

name: Carrefour
description: Founded in 1959, the Paris-based grocery retailer and wholesaler operates in more than 40 countries. The group is also present in numerous African, Middle Eastern, Central Asia and South Asian markets through local partner operators. Carrefour has been at the forefront of many now-familiar features of European retail, including hypermarkets, grocery e-commerce, and own-brand products, which now account for a significant portion of its food sales.

name: SK
description: Formerly known as SK Holdings Co., Ltd, SK Inc. was created when the company reorganized under a different structure in 2007. It is a holding company with different subsidiaries including SK Innovation and SK Telecom. It invests in advanced materials, biopharmaceuticals, energy (including electric-vehicle batteries), and digital businesses.

name: PepsiCo
description: PepsiCo, founded in 1965 through the merger of Pepsi-Cola and Frito-Lay, is a leading global food and beverage company. Headquartered in Purchase, N.Y., PepsiCo has a portfolio of brands that includes Pepsi, Mountain Dew, Lay’s, Gatorade, Tropicana, and Quaker. The company operates in more than 200 countries and territories.

name: Tencent Holdings
description: There’s having a dominating market presence, and then there’s what Tencent has with WeChat, the super-app that, among other things, serves as one of China’s two leading payment services. With 1.3 billion monthly active users, WeChat is ahead of rival Ant Group and its Alipay service. Now China’s platforms are tearing down their walls in part due to government pressure on the broader sector. In September 2024, Alibaba announced that WeChat users can now pay for things on the e-commerce company’s Taobao platform without ever leaving the Tencent app.

name: Christian Dior
description: Christian Dior SE is a France-based holding company that controls a significant portion of the multinational luxury conglomerate LVMH. Through a complex 2017 tie-up orchestrated by Bernard Arnault, who chairs both companies and serves as LVMH’s CEO, the combined group has a portfolio of leading brands in fashion, cosmetics and perfumes, watches and jewelry, wines and spirits, and luxury retail. These include Louis Vuitton, Fendi, Dior, Loewe, Celine, Givenchy, Bulgari, Tag Heuer, Veuve Clicquot, Hennessy, Glenmorangie and Guerlain. The group is also involved in luxury travel, retail (including Sephora, and the world’s first department store, Le Bon Marché Rive Gauche), yachts, art and media.

name: Walt Disney
description: Founded in 1923 as the Laugh-O-Gram Films studio, the Walt Disney Co. has grown into one of the world’s largest and most influential media conglomerates, with holdings that include ABC, ESPN, FX, and 20th Century Studios, as well as entertainment and media brands such as Pixar, Marvel Entertainment, Lucasfilm, and National Geographic. Disney’s streaming offerings include Disney+ and Hulu. Its Disney Experiences division oversees theme parks, resorts, and cruise lines around the world, as well as video games and merchandise.

name: UPS
description: United Parcel Service (UPS), founded in 1907, is a global giant in logistics, package delivery, and supply-chain management. Headquartered in Atlanta, UPS operates in more than 220 countries and territories, offering services ranging from shipping and freight to warehousing and distribution. The company is known for its distinctive brown delivery trucks and uniforms.

name: DHL Group
description: DHL Group, headquartered in Bonn, Germany, is Europe’s largest and one of the world’s leading logistics companies. Its modern form took shape when the privatized Deutsche Post acquired all shares of U.S.-based courier DHL by 2002, later merging and expanding under the DHL brand. While the group’s heritage, like that of other European postal services, is sometimes traced to medieval European postal services, its core businesses today are express delivery, global freight and forwarding, international logistics, supply chain services (including warehousing), and e-commerce solutions.

name: Crédit Agricole
description: France’s Crédit Agricole is a banking group with deep cooperative roots and a diverse presence across retail, corporate, and investment banking. Known for its strong network of regional banks, the group serves millions of clients worldwide. The company is headquartered in Montrouge.

name: Tesco
description: Tesco is a supermarket chain in the U.K., growing from a 1919 London market stall to commanding over a quarter of the country’s grocery market, with supermarkets and convenience stores in the U.K., plus stores across Ireland, the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Hungary. Tesco has also branched into telecoms (Tesco Mobile), banking (Tesco Bank) and data analytics consultancy.

name: Johnson & Johnson
description: Johnson & Johnson, founded in 1886, is among the world’s largest and most influential health care companies. It is involved in the research, development, manufacture, and distribution of innovative medicines and medical technologies. The company’s innovative medicine business operates in areas including oncology, immunology, neuroscience, and cardiopulmonary treatment. In medtech, the company is focused on developing and delivering cardiovascular, orthopedics, surgery, and vision solutions.

name: FedEx
description: FedEx, founded in 1971, is a multinational delivery services company known for its overnight shipping and pioneering tracking systems. Headquartered in Memphis, FedEx operates in more than 220 countries and territories, providing an array of services including express transportation, freight, e-commerce, and business solutions.

name: Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria
description: Multinational bank BBVA, founded in 1857, primarily focuses on retail banking, asset management, and wholesale and investment banking, with a smaller insurance division. It operates significantly in Spain, Mexico, Turkey, and South America. While BBVA originated in Bilbao, its main operational and corporate headquarters are located in Madrid, Spain, specifically in the Ciudad BBVA complex.

name: SAIC Motor
description: Founded in 1997, SAIC Motor is a subsidiary of Shanghai Automotive Industry Corporation (Group) Corp. It produces and sells vehicles in China and around the world. The company also enages in a myriad of other activities, including auto finance, research and development of technology, equity investment, and catering.

name: UBS Group
description: UBS is a global financial services firm headquartered in Zurich, specializing in wealth management, investment banking, asset management, and retail banking. Serving private, institutional, and corporate clients worldwide, the group delivers financial advice, capital market solutions, and sustainable investment strategies.

name: E.ON
description: German utility group E.ON operates primarily in the energy distribution and supply sector. The larger supplier side of the business is concentrated on Germany, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, along with 10 smaller markets, while the networks division mainly serves Germany. E.ON also provides EV charging points, heat pumps, smart meters for homes, as well as heating, cooling and on-site power supply for chemical firms, manufacturers, hospitals and real estate. The company is headquartered in Essen.

name: Archer Daniels Midland
description: Archer Daniels Midland (ADM), founded in 1902, is one of the largest global players in food processing and commodities trading. Headquartered in Chicago, ADM operates more than 800 facilities worldwide, processing oilseeds, corn, wheat, and other agricultural products. The company is a leading supplier of food ingredients, animal feed, and biofuels. ADM plays a crucial role in the global food supply chain, connecting crops to markets and providing essential ingredients to various industries.

name: Siemens
description: Germany’s Siemens is a technology powerhouse specializing in automation, digital industries, smart infrastructure, mobility and healthcare solutions. Siemens was founded in 1847 in Berlin where it maintains a registered office and today operates around the world from its official headquarters in Munich.

name: Enel
description: Headquartered in Rome, Enel is a leader in renewable energy and smart grid technologies, committed to decarbonization and innovation. It operates extensive wind, solar, hydro, and storage assets worldwide while investing heavily in grid modernization to support a sustainable energy transition.

name: Procter & Gamble
description: The consumer packaged goods company Procter & Gamble operates in five segments: beauty; grooming; health care; fabric and home care; and baby, feminine, and family care. Founded in 1837 when a British candlemaker and an Irish soapmaker merged their businesses in Cincinnati, its holdings include Tide, Pampers, Downy, Gillette, and Oral-B.

name: Lowe's
description: The home improvement retailer Lowe’s was founded in 1921. The brand operates 1,750 home improvement stores and employs approximately 200,000 associates. Its big-box stores, website, and app complete some 16 million customer transactions a week in the United States. Lowe’s sells DIY products, decor, tools, and gardening supplies, as well as raw materials for builders and contractors. It also sells appliances and electrical items, and offers installation services through independent contractors. Founded as a general store, Lowe’s pivoted to focusing entirely on home improvement in the 1940s, ahead of the postwar building boom, and is now the world’s second-largest home improvement retailer. It became a publicly traded company in 1961.

name: Energy Transfer
description: Founded in 1996, Energy Transfer owns and operates one of the largest and most diversified portfolios of energy assets in the United States, including natural gas storage facilities, more than 12,000 miles of intrastate natural gas transportation pipelines, and almost 21,000 miles of interstate natural gas pipelines. It offers natural gas compression services and carbon dioxide and hydrogen sulfide removal services, and manages coal and natural resources properties. It also sells standing timber, leases coal-related infrastructure facilities, sells and distributes gasoline, and has a limited partnership with the motor fuel company Sunoco.

name: Groupe BPCE
description: Groupe BPCE, based in Paris, was established in 2009 following the merger of two retail-focused French cooperative banking and insurance networks, Banque Populaire and Caisse d’Epargne, both with roots dating to the 19th century. While maintaining its strong retail banking presence, the group also operates globally through Natixis Investment Managers for asset and wealth management, as well as Natixis CIB for corporate and investment banking services.

name: RTX
description: RTX, an aerospace and defense company, provides systems and services for commercial, military, and government customers in the United States and internationally. It operates through three firms: Collins Aerospace, Pratt & Whitney, and Raytheon. The Collins Aerospace Systems segment designs, produces, and supports cabin interiors, including oxygen systems, food and beverage preparation, storage and galley systems, and lavatory and wastewater management systems; battlespace, test and training range systems, crew escape systems, and simulation and training solutions. Pratt & Whitney supplies aircraft engines for commercial, military, business jet, and general aviation customers; and produces, sells, and services military and commercial auxiliary power units. Raytheon provides defensive and offensive threat detection, tracking, and mitigation capabilities for U.S., foreign government, and commercial customers. The company, incorporated in 1934, was formerly known as Raytheon Technologies Corp. and changed its name to RTX Corp. in July 2023.

name: Albertsons
description: Albertsons, through its subsidiaries, operates food and drug stores in the United States. The company’s food and drug retail stores offer grocery products, general merchandise, health and beauty care products, pharmacy products, fuel, and other items and services. It operates stores under various brand names, including Albertsons, Safeway, Vons, Pavilions, Randalls, Tom Thumb, Carrs, Jewel-Osco, Acme, Shaw’s, Star Market, United Supermarkets, Market Street, Haggen, Kings Food Markets, and Balducci’s Food Lovers Market. In October 2022 Albertsons announced intentions to merge with Kroger in a $24.6 billion deal, but various unions and lawmakers mounted anticompetitive objections and the deal was ultimately blocked. Albertsons traces its roots back to 1860, the founding date of its Shaw’s brand; Albertsons currently operates as a subsidiary of Albertsons Investor Holdings LLC.

description: French energy giant Engie is one of Europe’s largest operators of gas distribution and storage infrastructure and a major generator and distributor of electricity. It is also heavily involved in the supply and trading of energy, the provision of on-site power, heating and cooling supply for businesses and districts, and the design and operation of power stations. In recent years, Engie’s major focus has been on expanding renewables and focusing on a smaller number of global markets.

description: Sysco is a marketer and distributor of food and related products to the food service or food-away-from-home industries in the U.S., Canada, the U.K., France, and elsewhere. The company serves restaurants, hospitals and nursing facilities, schools and colleges, hotels and motels, industrial caterers, and other food service venues. Sysco was incorporated in 1969 and is headquartered in Houston.

The company was founded in 1899 and operates in over 100 countries.

name: Progressive
description: Progressive provides insurance for a wide range of personal and business assets. The company is divided into three units. The personal division insures cars and recreational vehicles, while the commercial arm writes policies for businesses to cover their liability and vehicle fleets, including freight trucks. The third unit handles property insurance, including home and rental coverage. Progressive was founded in 1937.

name: Pertamina
description: A holding company since 2020, energy giant Pertamina has six integrated sub-holdings covering upstream, refining and petrochemical, gas, commercial and trading, marine logistics, and power and new renewable energy. In February 2025, Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto announced a new sovereign wealth fund, Danantara, which will take over several state-owned enterprises, including Pertamina.

name: Uniper
description: Outside of its home market of Germany, utility company Uniper operates in over 40 countries, with a particular focus on the Netherlands, Sweden and Britain. Its primary activity is gas procurement, trading and storage, alongside a diversification strategy that includes a growing LNG portfolio and renewables and hydrogen investments. It also provides business customers with carbon offsets and consultancy around decarbonization.

name: Airbus
description: Multinational aerospace giant Airbus is Europe’s leading producer of commercial aircraft. However, it also manufactures helicopters, military aircraft, satellites, and spacecraft components. In more recent years, the group—legally based in the Netherlands but run from France—has grown its services businesses, including cybersecurity, secure communications and data analytics, with customers including police, security services and emergency responders.

name: American Express
description: American Express is a global financial company that specializes in payment cards for consumers and businesses, as well as travel services. The company’s green charge card has the distinction of being the world’s first charge card to be made out of plastic, replacing the paper cards that were in use prior to its 1959 introduction. Amex was founded as a freight forwarding company in 1850. American Express Travelers Cheques, introduced in 1891, made it possible for people to obtain cash in foreign countries, changing the nature of travel and the company’s profile. Over its history, American Express has owned a cable TV business as well as an investment bank. The company is currently organized into four business segments: U.S. consumer services, international card services, commercial services, and global merchant and networking services.

name: Orlen
description: Orlen is a leading oil and gas producer, refiner, liquefied natural gas importer, power generator (gas and renewables-based), and distributor. Orlen is part-owned by the Polish state and is headquartered in Płock, Poland. The group is expanding into renewables and hydrogen, with the aim of deploying small nuclear reactors by 2035.

name: Deutsche Bank
description: Deutsche Bank gained its license from the Prussian government in 1870, with a particular focus on enabling trade between Germany and the rest of the world during rapid industrialization. It grew to become one of Europe’s foremost financial services companies. Today, it operates in four key areas: corporate banking, serving businesses from sole traders to multinationals under the Deutsche Bank, Postbank, and digital-only FYRST brands; investment banking; private banking, particularly within Germany; and asset management, under the DWS brand.

Lloyds is one of the U.K.’s largest banks and a major player in U.K. retail banking; it is also an insurance and pensions provider, with a commercial and investment banking division that leans towards SMEs. It is based in London and Edinburgh.

Some assets in the West have been divested or rebranded following the invasion of Ukraine and subsequent sanctions.

The group's products include savings, payments, investments, loans and mortgages in their retail markets and specialised lending, debt, equity market solutions and more for their wholesale banking.

name: Barclays
description: Barclays is one of Britain’s largest and oldest banks, tracing its origins to 1690. Its business is split into five distinct lines: a ring-fenced U.K. retail bank (including its Barclaycard credit division), a global investment bank, a U.K. SME and mid-cap-focused corporate bank, a private bank and wealth management division, and a U.S. consumer bank focused on co-branded and white label credit cards. The group is headquartered in London.

name: Lockheed Martin
description: Lockheed Martin is a global aerospace and security company involved in the research, design, and production of everything from jet fighters and missile defense systems to satellites and spacecraft. Lockheed Martin does the majority of its business with the U.S. Department of Defense and other federal agencies. Its roots go back to the early 20th century as an aircraft industry pioneer that became an important partner to the U.S. military during World War II. The modern company was formed in 1995 when Lockheed Corp. merged with Martin Marietta Corp., another large defense contractor.

name: MetLife
description: MetLife is one of the world’s largest providers of insurance, annuities, and employee benefits. Based in New York, MetLife sells insurance coverage through employers, offering life insurance, disability insurance, plus dental and vision plans. Founded in 1868 in the aftermath of the American Civil War, MetLife at one point became the nation’s largest life insurer. In 2017, MetLife stopped selling life insurance to individual policyholders in the U.S., spinning off its U.S. retail insurance business into a separate publicly listed company called Brighthouse Financial.

name: Roche Group
description: Swiss pharmaceutical giant Roche operates across a broad spectrum of drug treatment areas, with particular strength in oncology, immunology, neurology and infectious diseases. Its diagnostics division, which provides tests, instruments and digital tools for healthcare and medical researchers. The group was founded in 1896 by Fritz Hoffman-La Roche, whose descendants still have a controlling stake. Roche originally sold consumer-focused medicines like cough syrup, vitamins and Valium, and launched cosmetics business Pantene before selling it to Procter & Gamble. Roche is headquartered in Basel, Switzerland.

name: HCA Healthcare
description: HCA Healthcare owns many of the largest chains of hospitals, clinics, surgery centers, medical labs, and freestanding emergency rooms in the U.S., in addition to operating locations in the U.K. The company was founded in 1968 as one of the first U.S. hospital conglomerates. Since then, along with its industry rivals, it has undergone tremendous growth, partly through acquisitions of smaller health care chains.

name: BASF
description: German diversified chemicals group BASF is headquartered in Ludwigshafen, Germany and supplies petrochemicals and precursors for plastics, catalysts and battery materials for automotive, pesticides and herbicides for agriculture, biopolymers and surfactants for cosmetics, as well as vitamins and emulsifiers for food manufacturers. The group is the world's largest chemicals business outside of China, known for its broad portfolio supporting clients across global industries.

name: Koç Holding
description: Koç Holding is Turkey’s largest industrial conglomerate and investment holding company, with a global presence across energy, automotive, consumer durables, and finance. It stands out in finance and household appliances, particularly air conditioning and major white goods, while also maintaining smaller business segments in food retail, DIY, tourism, and information technology.

The company operates through its commercial airplanes; defense, space, and security; and global services segments. In recent years, safety concerns and labor disputes have plagued the company, which was once lauded for its engineering-first culture. Boeing was incorporated in 1916. After a long history outside Seattle, in 2001 it moved its headquarters to Chicago to be closer to customers. It ultimately moved again to Arlington, Va., where it’s presently headquartered.

description: Zurich is a leading Swiss insurance group, which was founded in 1872. Initially covering marine insurance, it rapidly expanded into a multi-line, global group offering life, pensions, investments, assurance, and property & casualty coverages. The group also operates a U.S.-based farming insurance business. Zurich is headquartered in its namesake city.

name: Unilever
description: British consumer goods giant Unilever operates a global, diverse portfolio, spanning food, personal care, home care, and beauty. Its well-known brands include Comfort, Marmite, Dove, Knorr, Hellmann’s, Sunsilk, Vaseline, Cif, and Lifebuoy. Formed in 1930 from the merger of British soapmaker Lever Brothers and Dutch margarine producer Margarine Unie, Unilever maintained dual nationality until it simplified its structure in 2020, establishing the U.K. as its single headquarters. The company continues to focus on premium segments of beauty, wellbeing, and personal care while maintaining a strong presence in food and home care products.

name: Accenture
description: Accenture is a global solutions and services company. Its broad range of offerings are roughly split between managed services and consulting, encompassing digital transformation, AI and data, cloud computing, cybersecurity, design and marketing, digital engineering and manufacturing, supply chain, and talent and organization. Accenture is incorporated in Dublin.

name: Caterpillar
description: Caterpillar is a global manufacturer of construction and mining equipment, industrial turbines, engines, and diesel-electric locomotives. Formed from the merger of two competitors in 1925, Caterpillar traces its origins to the fertile San Joaquin Valley, California’s agricultural heartland. The company’s name stems from one of the founders’ inventions, which replaced a steam tractor’s rear wheels with a track system that observers likened to a caterpillar as the machine crawled across soggy terrain. Caterpillar has seen its bright yellow machines become a familiar sight at construction sites around the world, while its employees develop products for industries ranging from oil and gas drilling and power generation to marine and rail technology.

name: Merck
description: New Jersey–based Merck was founded in 1891 as the American affiliate of a German parent. Today, as a stand-alone company, it is one of the world’s biggest pharmas by revenue. It has produced numerous blockbuster medications, including the cancer treatment branded as Keytruda, which was the world’s bestselling drug in 2023, earning Merck $25 billion that year. Other high-profile medications have included diabetes treatments and anti-HIV drugs. Merck produces vaccines and has a large animal medicine business as well as a services segment whose offerings include analytics and clinical services.

name: Allstate
description: Allstate provides a wide variety of insurance products—auto, home, and life among them—throughout the U.S. and Canada. When the firm, founded in 1931, went public in 1993—parent company Sears sold nearly 20% of its holdings—it was, at the time, the largest IPO in history. The company has been known since the 1950s for its slogan “You’re in good hands."

name: Pfizer
description: Pfizer is known for developing medications and vaccines, and for manufacturing them at dozens of factories around the world. Its treatments span a broad range of areas including oncology, rare diseases, inflammation and immunology, and vaccines. Oncology has become the company's primary strategic focus, with CEO Albert Bourla committing more than 40% of annual R&D spending to cancer research. Pfizer significantly expanded its cancer portfolio through its 2023 acquisition of Seagen, gaining a suite of antibody-drug conjugate therapies including Padcev for bladder cancer and Adcetris for lymphoma. The company is also making a major push into the obesity market: its late 2025 acquisition of Metsera brought Pfizer back into the obesity space after an earlier internal program was scrapped, positioning it to compete against dominant players Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly. During the COVID-19 pandemic, Pfizer developed a landmark and highly profitable vaccine in collaboration with the startup BioNTech; it also developed a treatment for COVID infections sold as Paxlovid. Pfizer was founded in 1849 by immigrants in New York City, which remains the site of its global headquarters.
