name: IBM
description: IBM is a cornerstone of U.S. business that is best known for its software, cloud computing services, and consulting. Incorporated in 1911, and later rebranded as International Business Machines, the company has ridden the many waves of innovation over the decades, from early technology such as tabulating machines, and time clocks for employee punch-ins, to today’s advancements in artificial intelligence. As of 2024, it was among just a few dozen companies to have appeared on the Fortune 500 every year since the list’s inception in 1955.

name: New York Life Insurance
description: New York Life is one of the oldest mutual life insurance companies in the U.S. Founded in 1845, it offers a range of insurance options, financial products, and advisory services, including retirement planning, wealth management, and investment offerings.

name: ArcelorMittal
description: Headquartered in Luxembourg, ArcelorMittal is one of the world’s largest vertically-integrated steel companies. Formed from the 2006 hostile takeover of European group Arcelor by India’s Mittal, the group’s steel production now largely takes place in Europe and North America, with iron and coking coal mining also taking place in South America, Africa and the former Soviet Union. The company is a major supplier of steel in various forms to the automotive and construction industries, but it also sells to packaging companies, appliance manufacturers and on the wholesale market.

name: Assicurazioni Generali
description: An integrated insurance and asset management group, Generali was founded in 1831 in Trieste, Italy. The company offers life and non-life insurance as well as a range of financial products and services.

name: Delta Air Lines
description: A fixture of the aviation world since it launched in the 1920s, Delta is one of the world’s largest airlines by passengers and by revenue. It has numerous U.S. hub cities, the biggest of which is Atlanta, where Delta is headquartered. The airline’s routes span most of the world, including Asia and Latin America. Delta’s iconic red triangle logo is suggestive of flight and the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet. The airline also helped popularize Biscoff cookies—the name a portmanteau of biscuit and coffee—as an in-flight snack.

Publix has won dozens of awards for how well it treats both its customers and its employees. The grocery chain places a big emphasis on improving corporate culture, including such efforts as Be There Day, when leadership team members choose a day to work alongside associates in other departments to learn more about their respective contributions.

name: Edeka Zentrale

name: Daimler Truck Holding
description: Daimler Truck Holding is a leading manufacturer of commercial vehicles, producing a wide range of trucks and buses under brands such as Mercedes-Benz and Setra. Its business encompasses cloud services, cybersecurity, analytics, AI, the Internet of Things, and a variety of other “as a service” products. It sells to other companies but also to the public sector. Customers include the U.S. government and state and local governments, as well as education, health care, and utility markets. description: The corporate history of ConocoPhillips traces back to 1875, when early precursors of today’s energy giant transported kerosene by rail to pioneers in the Mountain West. The firm’s current name comes from a 2002 merger between Phillips Petroleum and Conoco. Headquartered in Houston, ConocoPhillips extracts, processes, and transports a variety of fuels, including petroleum, natural gas, and bitumen. The company has operations in more than a dozen countries, with the bulk of its production in the United States, particularly Alaska. Other sites of production include Canada, Norway, Australia, and Southeast Asia.

name: AbbVie
description: AbbVie is among the largest pharmaceutical companies by revenue, and provides therapeutic solutions in areas including immunology, oncology, neuroscience, and eye care. AbbVie was founded in 2013 as a spinoff from Abbott Laboratories and is best known for blockbuster drugs like Botox and Humira, one of the world’s top-selling pharmaceuticals.

name: Enterprise Products Partners
description: Enterprise Products Partners processes, transports, stores, and ships oil and natural gas products across the United States. Enterprise is a "midstream” energy company, meaning it connects the producers of oil and gas with distributors and retailers. The company oversees about 50,000 miles of pipelines, most originating in Louisiana and Texas. It also owns shipping docks and storage facilities for the export of oil and gas products, and natural gas processing facilities. Founded in 1965, Enterprise Products is based in Houston.

The company sells a wide range of products including frozen food, candy, cigarettes, and beauty items. PFG engages with a variety of businesses, from small independent restaurants to large institutions like hospitals.

name: American Airlines Group
description: One of the largest airlines in the world, American Airlines transports both passengers and cargo through major cities including Los Angeles, Madrid, and Tokyo. name: AstraZeneca
description: AstraZeneca is a British-Swedish pharmaceutical and biotechnology company headquartered in Cambridge, U.K. Formed in 1999 through the merger of Swedish Astra AB and British Zeneca Group, it is one of the largest drug companies known for pioneering medicines, including treatment for lung cancer and the development of a widely distributed COVID-19 vaccine.

name: Capital One Financial
description: Capital One is a bank and issuer of credit cards, founded in 1994 and based in Virginia. As of 2024 it was the third-largest issuer of Visa and Mastercard credit cards in the U.S. Capital One also offers a range of banking services, including consumer and commercial loans, and has 259 retail locations. In May 2025, Capital One completed the acquisition of Discover Financial Services, agreed to in 2024, in a stock transaction valued at $35.3 billion. The resulting company is now one of the world’s largest credit card issuers, with more than 100 million customers.

name: Cisco Systems
description: Cisco is a global provider of networking infrastructure, designing and building everything from routers and wireless access points to the software that’s used to secure them. Founded in 1984 by a team of Stanford computer scientists, Cisco went public in 1990 and was added to the Dow Jones industrial average in 2009. Cisco made a flurry of acquisitions in the 2010s and into the 2020s. It closed in March 2024 on a $28 billion deal for Splunk, a cybersecurity and analytics firm, as part of a larger bet on companies adopting AI.

name: Rio Tinto Group
description: Founded in 1873, Rio Tinto began when a group of British and European investors acquired a mine complex along the Rio Tinto River in Huelva, Spain, from the Spanish government. It is now a leading mining and metals company operating in 35 countries, with a diverse portfolio that includes iron ore, copper, aluminum, and more.

name: HP
description: HP was formed when the company originally known as Hewlett-Packard split into two distinct businesses in 2015: Hewlett Packard Enterprise and HP. The company operates in three parts: The first is personal systems, including desktop and notebook PCs, retail point-of-sale systems, as well as related software products. The second is printing, including printer hardware and supplies. The third is corporate investments, which includes business incubation. HP serves a range of clients from individual consumers to large enterprises.

name: Phoenix Pharma
description: Phoenix Group is a pharmaceutical wholesaler and pharmacy retailer, supplying medicines and healthcare products globally. The company is working to achieve CO2 neutrality in its operations by 2030.

name: Sanofi
description: Sanofi is a global biopharma company headquartered in Paris, France. The company specializes in innovative medicines and vaccines for major diseases, driven by research and AI technology.

name: Tyson Foods
description: Founded in 1935, Tyson is a global food company that operates in four segments: prepared foods, pork, chicken, and beef. It processes live farm animals, manufactures frozen food, and sells products to retailers and wholesalers.

name: Bunge Global
description: Bunge Global is a player in the global agribusiness and food sector, headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. The company specializes in sourcing, processing, trading oilseeds and grains, producing protein meal for animal feed and edible oils for food processing and biofuels. Bunge serves customers worldwide along the farm-to-consumer food chain.

name: Intel
description: Intel is one of the largest semiconductor chip makers in the world. Founded in 1968, it designs, develops, manufactures, markets, and sells computing and related products and services.

name: Oracle
description: Founded in 1977, Oracle is a multinational technology company that builds and sells products and services that address enterprise technology environments. It provides database software, cloud computing technology, and development tools. It also provides hardware products and hardware-related software products. The company markets and sells its cloud, license, hardware, and support offerings directly to businesses, government agencies, and educational institutions.

name: Broadcom
description: Founded in 1961, Broadcom operates in two segments: One is focused on developing and supplying semiconductors, including chips for artificial intelligence. The other provides infrastructure, including Ethernet switching and routing and fiber-optic transmitter and receiver components. The company also offers components for Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and global positioning systems. Its products are used in various applications in enterprise and data center networking, including artificial intelligence networking and connectivity. Google, Meta, ByteDance, and OpenAI are among Broadcom’s customers for its custom AI chips.

The bank is a key player in Russia’s financial sector with a strategic focus on sustainability and innovation, serving millions of customers worldwide.

name: Novartis
description: Novartis is a Swiss multinational pharmaceutical company headquartered in Basel, Switzerland. Formed in 1996 through the merger of Ciba-Geigy and Sandoz, the company's medicines reach 296 million people worldwide.

name: Deere
description: Deere (commonly known as John Deere) is an agricultural giant that manufactures and sells tractors, harvesters, loaders, and other equipment used by farmers worldwide. Founded in 1837 as a maker of steel plows pulled by horses, the company has expanded into heavy machinery used for golf course maintenance, snow removal, and logging. The company introduced a self-driving tractor in 2022 and is pushing into machine learning to help increase agricultural production. As of 2024, it was among a small number of companies that have been on the Fortune 500 every year since the list’s inception in 1955.
